title: I Tell You That Grief Without Hope Is Grief Without Passion...
text:
I tell you that grief without hope is grief without passion,

and that only unbelieving men feel pain,

snatched up by anguish, in the night air,

rising toward God's throne shouting spells.

A desert full of souls, naked silence lies

beneath the snowy, vertical eye of absolute Heaven.

The deep-hearted man expresses grief

for his dead in the quietest silence, mute,

like an enormous statue raised in eternal stone,

not moving until he himself lies in the earth.

Touch them: the marble of their eyes never grows wet,

for if it could weep, it might arise and disappear.
editorial_note: This first-line variant keeps the same English rendering as the matching Browning grief entry.

title: The Face of the World Has Changed
text:
The face of the world has changed

since I heard the steps of your soul, light,

oh, very light!, beside me, slipping

between me and the terrible cleft of death

where I thought I would sink, but I was lifted

toward love and came to know a new song

to rock the tides of life.

Thirsty, I drained the cup of bitterness

that God, at birth, gives us;

beside you, my love, I have praised its sweetness.

The names of lands and sky are altered,

they change according to where you are

or may someday be.

Before, I adored this lute and this song of mine

(the angels know it well); I still love them,

only because your name mingles with their rhythm.
editorial_note: The translation keeps this Spanish variant's fuller music-and-tide phrasing.

title: Do Not Accuse Me, I Beg You
text:
Do not accuse me, I beg you, for the excessive calm

or sadness of my face when I am beside you,

for we look toward opposite places, and one same sun

cannot gild both our brows and hair.


You always look at me without anguish or doubt, as

at a bee enclosed in a crystal urn,

for suffering keeps me in a temple of love,

and for me to spread my wings and fly through the air


would be an impossible failure, if I

wished to try it. But when I look at you, I already see

the end of all love beside the love of now;


beyond memory I already hear forgetting,

like one who, resting on a height, contemplates

beyond the rivers the bitter sea stretched out.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the two lovers' unequal perspective and the bitter sea beyond memory.

title: I Never Gave a Lock of My Hair to Any Man
text:
I never gave a lock of my hair to any man,

my beloved, except the one I offer you now,

and, thoughtfully, along all its somber

length, I wind it around my fingers.


Take it. My days of youth have passed;

my hair no longer trembles at my joyful step,

nor do I fasten in it the rose or myrtle shoots,

as girls usually do: now it can only, on pale


cheeks, shade the traces of my weeping,

and it has grown used to coming loose when sorrow,

with its art, bends the forehead. I feared the funereal


scissors would cut it first, and your

love has prevailed. Take it. Pure as before, you will find

the kiss my mother left in it when she died.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the lock of hair as intimate gift, mourning relic, and maternal trace.

title: Go Away from Me
text:
Go away from me. Yet I know that, forever,

I must remain in your shadow. Never again, solitary,

standing on the very thresholds of my hidden

life, will I be able to govern the impulses


of my soul, or raise my hand as before

to the sun, serenely, without perceiving in it

what until now I tried to put aside: the touch

of your hand in mine. This broad earth


with which fate wished to separate us, in my own fate

leaves your heart, with double beating. In everything

I do or dream you are present, as


in wine the taste of grapes. And when

I pray to the Lord for myself, in my prayers He hears

your name and sees our tears mingle in my eyes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradox of separation: distance only deepens the beloved's presence.
